content: {"summary":"The lag of ~54,000 messages on notifications.outbound at 18:30 UTC on 29 June 2026 was due to a slowdown of the external email provider’s API, not because messages were removed from the topic. Retention for the topic was the default 168 hours (7 days) with no override, and the oldest unread message was far from the retention limit, so no deletions occurred before workers could read them.","likely_cause":"External email provider API slowdown caused send latency, creating a backlog in notifications.outbound.","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"Messages were not deleted before workers read them because the topic used the default 7‑day retention and the backlog was far from that limit.","evidence_ids":["INC-0171#0","INC-0171#2"],"quote":"notifications.outbound has no retention override, so it keeps the broker default of 168 h"},{"text":"The backlog grew because the email provider’s API answered slowly, reducing send throughput and increasing consumer lag.","evidence_ids":["INC-0171#0","INC-0171#1"],"quote":"the email provider's API starts answering slowly; consumer lag ... begins to climb"}],"next_checks":["Verify that the retention setting for notifications.outbound remains at the default 168 hours and that no overrides have been added since the incident.","Monitor consumer lag against retention thresholds to ensure backlog never approaches the retention limit.","Check Kafka broker disk usage and partition sizes for notifications.outbound to confirm sufficient capacity for future spikes.","Confirm with the email provider that their API performance issue has been resolved and obtain any post‑mortem details."]}
